question: What does “víz” mean?
explanation: “víz” means “water”. “bread” is kenyér and “milk” is tej. Literally: Kérek egy pohár vizet. = “ask-I a glass water-ACC”.

question: What does “kenyér” mean?
explanation: “kenyér” means “bread”. “cheese” is sajt and “butter” is vaj. Literally: A kenyér friss. = “the bread fresh”.

question: What does “alma” mean?
explanation: “alma” means “apple”. “pear” is körte and “plum” is szilva. Literally: Szeretem az almát. = “love-I the apple-ACC”.

question: What does “tej” mean?
explanation: “tej” means “milk”. “water” is víz and “beer” is sör. Literally: Reggelire tejet iszom. = “breakfast-for milk-ACC drink-I”.

question: What does “kávé” mean?
explanation: “kávé” means “coffee”. “tea” is tea and “juice” is gyümölcslé. Literally: Egy kávét kérek. = “a coffee-ACC ask-I”.

question: What does “kutya” mean?
explanation: “kutya” means “dog”. “cat” is macska and “horse” is ló. Literally: A kutya nagy. = “the dog big”.

question: What does “macska” mean?
explanation: “macska” means “cat”. “mouse” is egér and “bird” is madár. Literally: A macska alszik. = “the cat sleeps”.

question: What does “ház” mean?
explanation: “ház” means “house”. “door” is ajtó and “window” is ablak. Literally: Ez a ház szép. = “this the house beautiful”.

question: What does “ajtó” mean?
explanation: “ajtó” means “door”. “wall” is fal and “window” is ablak. Literally: Nyisd ki az ajtót! = “open out the door-ACC”.

question: What does “asztal” mean?
explanation: “asztal” means “table”. “chair” is szék and “bed” is ágy. Literally: A könyv az asztalon van. = “the book the table-on is”.

question: What does “szék” mean?
explanation: “szék” means “chair”. “lamp” is lámpa and “carpet” is szőnyeg. Literally: Ülj le a székre! = “sit down the chair-onto”.

question: What does “könyv” mean?
explanation: “könyv” means “book”. “pen” is toll and “notebook” is füzet. Literally: Olvasok egy könyvet. = “read-I a book-ACC”.

question: What does “toll” mean?
explanation: “toll” means “pen”. “pencil” is ceruza and “eraser” is radír. Toll also means “feather”. Literally: Van tollad? = “is pen-your”.

question: What does “iskola” mean?
explanation: “iskola” means “school”. “shop” is bolt and “hospital” is kórház. Literally: Az iskola nyolckor kezdődik. = “the school eight-at begins”.

question: What does “bolt” mean?
explanation: “bolt” means “shop”. “bank” is bank and “post office” is posta. Literally: A bolt nyitva van. = “the shop open is”.

question: What does “kórház” mean?
explanation: “kórház” means “hospital”. “restaurant” is étterem and “library” is könyvtár. Literally: A kórház messze van. = “the hospital far is”.

question: What does “étterem” mean?
explanation: “étterem” means “restaurant”. “hotel” is szálloda and “museum” is múzeum. Literally: Az étterem jó. = “the restaurant good”.

question: What does “barát” mean?
explanation: “barát” means “friend”. “neighbour” is szomszéd and “teacher” is tanár. Literally: Ő a barátom. = “he/she the friend-my”.

question: What does “anya” mean?
explanation: “anya” means “mother”. “father” is apa and “older sister” is nővér. Literally: Az anyám tanár. = “the mother-my teacher”.

question: What does “apa” mean?
explanation: “apa” means “father”. “boy / son” is fiú and “girl / daughter” is lány. Literally: Apa dolgozik. = “dad works”.

question: What does “testvér” mean?
explanation: “testvér” means “sibling”. “cousin” is unokatestvér and “neighbour” is szomszéd. Literally: Van egy testvérem. = “is a sibling-my”.

question: What does “piros” mean?
explanation: “piros” means “red”. “blue” is kék and “green” is zöld. Literally: A busz piros. = “the bus red”.

question: What does “kék” mean?
explanation: “kék” means “blue”. “yellow” is sárga and “black” is fekete. Literally: Az ég kék. = “the sky blue”.

question: What does “fehér” mean?
explanation: “fehér” means “white”. “grey” is szürke and “brown” is barna. Literally: A hó fehér. = “the snow white”.

question: What does “nagy” mean?
explanation: “nagy” means “big”. “small” is kicsi and “cold” is hideg. Literally: Nagy a város. = “big the city”.

question: What does “kicsi” mean?
explanation: “kicsi” means “small”. “long” is hosszú and “fast” is gyors. Literally: Kicsi a lakás. = “small the flat”.

question: What does “meleg” mean?
explanation: “meleg” means “warm / hot”. “cold” is hideg and “wet” is nedves. Literally: Ma meleg van. = “today warm is”.

question: What does “gyors” mean?
explanation: “gyors” means “fast”. “slow” is lassú and “heavy” is nehéz. Literally: A vonat gyors. = “the train fast”.

question: What does “szép” mean?
explanation: “szép” means “beautiful”. “ugly” is csúnya and “tired” is fáradt. Literally: Szép napunk van. = “beautiful day-our is”.

question: What does “éhes” mean?
explanation: “éhes” means “hungry”. “thirsty” is szomjas and “tired” is fáradt. Literally: Éhes vagyok. = “hungry am-I”.

question: What does “fáradt” mean?
explanation: “fáradt” means “tired”. “happy” is boldog and “sad” is szomorú. Literally: Nagyon fáradt vagyok. = “very tired am-I”.

question: What does “enni” mean?
explanation: “enni” means “to eat”. “to drink” is inni and “to sleep” is aludni. Literally: Enni szeretnék. = “eat-to like-would-I”.

question: What does “inni” mean?
explanation: “inni” means “to drink”. “to eat” is enni and “to cook” is főzni. Literally: Mit szeretnél inni? = “what-ACC like-would-you drink-to”.

question: What does “menni” mean?
explanation: “menni” means “to go”. “to come” is jönni and “to stay” is maradni. Literally: Haza akarok menni. = “home want-I go-to”.

question: What does “olvasni” mean?
explanation: “olvasni” means “to read”. “to write” is írni and “to speak” is beszélni. Literally: Szeretek olvasni. = “like-I read-to”.

question: What does “tanulni” mean?
explanation: “tanulni” means “to learn / study”. “to teach” is tanítani and “to work” is dolgozni. Literally: Magyarul tanulok. = “Hungarian-in learn-I”.

question: What does “reggeli” mean?
explanation: “reggeli” means “breakfast”. “lunch” is ebéd and “dinner” is vacsora. Literally: A reggeli nyolckor van. = “the breakfast eight-at is”.

question: What does “busz” mean?
explanation: “busz” means “bus”. “train” is vonat and “plane” is repülő. Literally: A busz későn jön. = “the bus late comes”.

question: What does “vonat” mean?
explanation: “vonat” means “train”. “bus” is busz and “tram” is villamos. Literally: A vonat Budapestre megy. = “the train Budapest-to goes”.

question: What does “repülőtér” mean?
explanation: “repülőtér” means “airport”. “railway station” is pályaudvar and “harbour” is kikötő. Literally: A repülőtér messze van. = “the airport far is”.

question: What does “város” mean?
explanation: “város” means “city”. “village” is falu and “street” is utca. Literally: Budapest nagy város. = “Budapest big city”.

question: What does “utca” mean?
explanation: “utca” means “street”. “square” is tér and “bridge” is híd. Literally: Melyik utca ez? = “which street this”.

question: What does “pénz” mean?
explanation: “pénz” means “money”. “price” is ár and “card” is kártya. Literally: Nincs pénzem. = “not-is money-my”.

question: What does “drága” mean?
explanation: “drága” means “expensive”. “cheap” is olcsó and “free of charge” is ingyen. Literally: Ez túl drága. = “this too expensive”.

question: What does “eső” mean?
explanation: “eső” means “rain”. “snow” is hó and “wind” is szél. Literally: Esik az eső. = “falls the rain”.

question: What does “fej” mean?
explanation: “fej” means “head”. “hand” is kéz and “leg / foot” is láb. Literally: Fáj a fejem. = “hurts the head-my”.

question: What does “kéz” mean?
explanation: “kéz” means “hand”. “eye” is szem and “ear” is fül. Literally: Mosd meg a kezed! = “wash PREVERB the hand-your”.

question: What does “szem” mean?
explanation: “szem” means “eye”. “nose” is orr and “mouth” is száj. Literally: Kék a szeme. = “blue the eye-his/her”.

question: What does “orvos” mean?
explanation: “orvos” means “doctor”. “teacher” is tanár and “driver” is sofőr. Literally: Az orvos kedves. = “the doctor kind”.

question: What does “tanár” mean?
explanation: “tanár” means “teacher”. “student” is diák and “doctor” is orvos. Literally: A tanár magyar. = “the teacher Hungarian”.

question: What does “Szia!” mean?
explanation: “Szia!” means “Hi! / Bye! (informal)”. “Thank you” is Köszönöm and “Sorry” is Bocsánat. Literally: Szia, Anna! = “hi, Anna”.

question: What does “Köszönöm.” mean?
explanation: “Köszönöm.” means “Thank you.”. “Please” is Kérem and “You're welcome” is Szívesen. Literally: Köszönöm szépen! = “thank-I nicely”.

question: What does “Jó reggelt!” mean?
explanation: “Jó reggelt!” means “Good morning!”. “Good evening” is Jó estét and “Good night” is Jó éjszakát. Literally: Jó reggelt kívánok! = “good morning-ACC wish-I”.

question: What does “Hogy vagy?” mean?
explanation: “Hogy vagy?” means “How are you?”. “What's your name?” is Hogy hívnak? and “Where are you from?” is Honnan jössz?. Literally: Hogy vagy? = “how are-you”.

question: What does “Hogy hívnak?” mean?
explanation: “Hogy hívnak?” means “What's your name?”. “How are you?” is Hogy vagy? and “How old are you?” is Hány éves vagy?. Literally: Hogy hívnak? = “how call-they-you”.

question: What does “Honnan jössz?” mean?
explanation: “Honnan jössz?” means “Where are you from?”. “Where are you going?” is Hová mész? and “What do you do?” is Mit csinálsz?. Literally: Honnan jössz? = “where-from come-you”.

question: What does “Nem értem.” mean?
explanation: “Nem értem.” means “I don't understand.”. “I don't know.” is Nem tudom. and “I don't want it.” is Nem akarom.. Literally: Nem értem. = “not understand-I”.

question: What does “Elnézést!” mean?
explanation: “Elnézést!” means “Excuse me! / Sorry!”. “Goodbye” is Viszlát and “Good night” is Jó éjszakát. Literally: Elnézést! = “forbearance-ACC”.

question: What does “Szívesen.” mean?
explanation: “Szívesen.” means “You're welcome.”. “Thank you” is Köszönöm and “Please” is Kérem. Literally: Szívesen. = “gladly”.

question: What does “Jó éjszakát!” mean?
explanation: “Jó éjszakát!” means “Good night!”. “Good morning” is Jó reggelt and “Good evening” is Jó estét. Literally: Jó éjszakát! = “good night-ACC”.

question: What does “Viszlát!” mean?
explanation: “Viszlát!” means “Goodbye!”. “Hello (formal)” is Jó napot and “Thank you” is Köszönöm. Literally: Viszlát! = “see-you-again (short for viszontlátásra)”.

question: What does “Mennyibe kerül?” mean?
explanation: “Mennyibe kerül?” means “How much does it cost?”. “What time is it?” is Hány óra van? and “Where is it?” is Hol van?. Literally: Mennyibe kerül? = “how-much-into costs”.

question: What does “Hol van a vécé?” mean?
explanation: “Hol van a vécé?” means “Where is the toilet?”. “Where is the shop?” is Hol van a bolt? and “What is this?” is Mi ez?. Literally: Hol van a vécé? = “where is the toilet”.

question: What does “Beszélsz angolul?” mean?
explanation: “Beszélsz angolul?” means “Do you speak English?”. “Do you speak Hungarian?” is Beszélsz magyarul? and “Do you understand?” is Érted?. Literally: Beszélsz angolul? = “speak-you English-in”.

question: What does “Segítség!” mean?
explanation: “Segítség!” means “Help!”. “Stop!” is Állj! and “Fire!” is Tűz!. Literally: Segítség! = “help / assistance”.

question: What does “Jó étvágyat!” mean?
explanation: “Jó étvágyat!” means “Enjoy your meal!”. “Cheers!” is Egészségedre and “Good luck!” is Sok sikert. Literally: Jó étvágyat! = “good appetite-ACC”.

question: What does “Egészségedre!” mean?
explanation: “Egészségedre!” means “Cheers! / Bless you!”. “Enjoy your meal” is Jó étvágyat and “Good luck” is Sok sikert. Literally: Egészségedre! = “health-your-onto”.

question: What does “Boldog születésnapot!” mean?
explanation: “Boldog születésnapot!” means “Happy birthday!”. “Happy New Year” is Boldog új évet and “Merry Christmas” is Boldog karácsonyt. Literally: Boldog születésnapot! = “happy birthday-ACC”.

question: What does “hét” mean?
explanation: “hét” means “seven”. “six” is hat and “eight” is nyolc. Hét also means “week”. Literally: Egy hétben hét nap van. = “one week-in seven day is”.

question: What does “húsz” mean?
explanation: “húsz” means “twenty”. “ten” is tíz and “thirty” is harminc. Literally: Húsz éves vagyok. = “twenty year-old am-I”.

question: What does “száz” mean?
explanation: “száz” means “one hundred”. “one thousand” is ezer and “ten” is tíz. Literally: Száz forint. = “hundred forint”.

question: What does “hétfő” mean?
explanation: “hétfő” means “Monday”. “Sunday” is vasárnap and “Friday” is péntek. Literally: Hétfőn dolgozom. = “Monday-on work-I”.

question: What does “szombat” mean?
explanation: “szombat” means “Saturday”. “Sunday” is vasárnap and “Wednesday” is szerda. Literally: Szombaton nem dolgozom. = “Saturday-on not work-I”.

question: What does “tegnap” mean?
explanation: “tegnap” means “yesterday”. “today” is ma and “tomorrow” is holnap. Literally: Tegnap esett az eső. = “yesterday fell the rain”.

question: What does “óra” mean?
explanation: “óra” means “hour / clock / o'clock”. “minute” is perc and “day” is nap. Literally: Hány óra van? = “how-many hour is”.

question: What does “reggel” mean?
explanation: “reggel” means “morning”. “evening” is este and “night” is éjszaka. Literally: Reggel kávét iszom. = “morning coffee-ACC drink-I”.

question: What does “ő” mean?
explanation: Hungarian has no grammatical gender, so ő covers both “he” and “she”. “We” is mi and “they” is ők. Literally: Ő itt lakik. = “he/she here lives”.

question: How do you say “He is a teacher”?
explanation: With he/she/it and they, “is/are” (van/vannak) is dropped before a noun or adjective. Vagyok belongs to én (I). Literally: Ő tanár. = “he/she teacher”.

question: Complete: “Én diák ___.” (I am a student)
explanation: Present of lenni: vagyok (I am), vagy (you are), van (he/she is). Literally: Én diák vagyok. = “I student am-I”.

question: Complete: “Te magyar ___?” (Are you Hungarian?)
explanation: Vagy = you are, vagyok = I am, vagyunk = we are. Literally: Te magyar vagy? = “you Hungarian are-you”.

question: Which word means “the” in “___ alma” (the apple)?
explanation: Use az before a vowel sound and a before a consonant. Egy means “a/an”. Literally: Az alma piros. = “the apple red”.

question: What is the plural of “könyv” (book)?
explanation: Plurals add -k with a linking vowel chosen by vowel harmony. Könyv has a front vowel (ö), so it takes -ek. Literally: A könyvek az asztalon vannak. = “the book-PL the table-on are-they”.

question: What is the plural of “ház” (house)?
explanation: Ház has a back vowel (á), so it takes -ak. Literally: A házak nagyok. = “the house-PL big-PL”.

question: How do you say “two books”?
explanation: After a number the noun stays singular. Két is used before a noun; kettő stands alone. Literally: Két kávét kérek. = “two coffee-ACC ask-I”.

question: How do you say “I eat an apple”?
explanation: A direct object takes the accusative ending -t (alma → almát). Almán would mean “on the apple”. Literally: Eszem egy almát. = “eat-I an apple-ACC”.

question: How do you say “I see the book”?
explanation: A definite object (“the book”) triggers the definite conjugation: látom. An indefinite object uses látok (Látok egy könyvet). The object also needs -et. Literally: Látom a könyvet. = “see-I(DEF) the book-ACC”.

question: How do you say “in the house”?
explanation: -ban/-ben = in, -on/-en/-ön = on, -hoz/-hez/-höz = to (someone/something). Literally: A kutya a házban van. = “the dog the house-in is”.

question: How do you say “on the table”?
explanation: -on/-en/-ön marks “on”. Asztalban = in the table and asztalhoz = to the table. Literally: A könyv az asztalon van. = “the book the table-on is”.

question: How do you say “I'm going to the city”?
explanation: -ba/-be = into/to, -ban/-ben = in, -ból/-ből = out of/from. Movement towards uses -ba/-be. Literally: Megyek a városba. = “go-I the city-into”.

question: How do you say “my book”?
explanation: Possessive suffixes: -m = my, -d = your, -a/-e = his/her. Literally: A könyvem az asztalon van. = “the book-my the table-on is”.

question: How do you say “I have a dog”?
explanation: Hungarian has no verb “to have”: it says “there is my dog”. The suffix shows the owner: kutyám (my), kutyád (your), kutyája (his/her). Literally: Van egy kutyám. = “is a dog-my”.

question: How do you say “There is no water”?
explanation: Nincs is nem + van and means “there isn't / (he) hasn't”. Nem víz means “it's not water”. Literally: Nincs víz. = “isn't water”.

question: How do you say “I'm not hungry”?
explanation: Put nem before the verb or word it negates. Nem vagy éhes = you aren't hungry; Nem éhes = he/she isn't hungry. Literally: Nem vagyok éhes. = “not am-I hungry”.

question: What does “miért” mean?
explanation: Miért = why, mikor = when, hogyan = how. Literally: Miért vagy fáradt? = “why are-you tired”.

question: Which word means “where to”?
explanation: Hol = where (location), hová = where to (direction), honnan = where from. Literally: Hová mész? = “where-to go-you”.

question: Complete: “Te kenyeret ___.” (You eat bread)
explanation: Enni (iksz verb): eszem (I), eszel (you), eszik (he/she). Literally: Te kenyeret eszel. = “you bread-ACC eat-you”.

question: Complete: “Ők a boltba ___.” (They are going to the shop)
explanation: Menni is irregular: megyek (I), mész (you), megy (he/she), megyünk (we), mentek (you pl.), mennek (they). Literally: Ők a boltba mennek. = “they the shop-into go-they”.

question: Complete: “Tegnap ___.” (Yesterday I worked)
explanation: The past tense adds -t- and a personal ending: dolgoztam (I worked). Dolgozom = I work, dolgozni = to work. Literally: Tegnap dolgoztam. = “yesterday worked-I”.

question: What does “volt” mean?
explanation: Volt is the past of van (was). Lesz = will be and van = is. Literally: Tegnap otthon voltam. = “yesterday at-home was-I”.

question: What does “lesz” mean?
explanation: Lesz is the future of van (will be). Volt = was and van = is. Literally: Holnap hideg lesz. = “tomorrow cold will-be”.

question: Tedd a könyvet az asztal___! (Put the book on the table)
explanation: -ra/-re means “onto” (movement); -on/-en/-ön means “on” (location). Literally: Tedd a könyvet az asztalra! = “put the book-ACC the table-onto!”.

question: Mesélek a családom___. (I'm telling you about my family)
explanation: -ról/-ről means “about / off”. Literally: Mesélek a családomról. = “tell-I the family-my-about”.

question: Busz___ megyek munkába. (I go to work by bus)
explanation: -val/-vel (“with / by”) assimilates to a final consonant: busz + val → busszal. Literally: Buszszal megyek munkába. = “bus-by go-I work-into”.

question: Moziba megyek ___. (I'm going to the cinema with Anna)
explanation: Final -a lengthens to -á before a suffix, and -val/-vel means “with”: Annával. Literally: Moziba megyek Annával. = “cinema-into go-I Anna-with”.

question: A barátom___ alszom ma este. (I'm sleeping at my friend's place tonight)
explanation: -nál/-nél means “at (someone's place)”. Literally: A barátomnál alszom ma este. = “the friend-my-at sleep-I today evening”.

question: Levelet kaptam a testvérem___. (I got a letter from my sibling)
explanation: -tól/-től means “from (a person)”; testvérem has front vowels, so -től. Literally: Levelet kaptam a testvéremtől. = “letter-ACC got-I the sibling-my-from”.

question: Megyek az orvos___. (I'm going to the doctor)
explanation: -hoz/-hez/-höz means “to (a person)”; orvos has back vowels, so -hoz. Literally: Megyek az orvoshoz. = “go-I the doctor-to”.

question: A szobá___ vagyok. (I'm in the room)
explanation: -ban/-ben means “in”; szoba has back vowels, so -ban (and a lengthens to á). Literally: A szobában vagyok. = “the room-in am-I”.

question: Tegnap este sokat ___. (Last night I read a lot)
explanation: Past tense: -t- + personal ending (olvas → olvastam). Literally: Tegnap este sokat olvastam. = “yesterday evening much-ACC read-I”.

question: Ő tegnap moziban ___. (She was at the cinema yesterday)
explanation: Volt is the past of van (was). Literally: Ő tegnap moziban volt. = “he/she yesterday cinema-in was”.

question: Tegnap mi sokat ___. (Yesterday we walked a lot)
explanation: Past tense, “we”: -t- + -unk/-ünk: sétáltunk. Literally: Tegnap mi sokat sétáltunk. = “yesterday we much walked-we”.

question: Holnap dolgozni ___. (I will work tomorrow)
explanation: The future = fog + infinitive; fogok is the “I” form. Literally: Holnap dolgozni fogok. = “tomorrow work-to will-I”.

question: Tudok ___. (I can swim)
explanation: After tudok (I can), use the infinitive: úszni. Literally: Tudok úszni. = “can-I swim-to”.

question: Kávét ___ szeretnék. (I'd like to drink coffee)
explanation: Szeretnék (I'd like) is followed by the infinitive: inni. Literally: Kávét inni szeretnék. = “coffee-ACC drink-to like-would-I”.

question: Ismered ___ a lányt? (Do you know that girl?)
explanation: A demonstrative before a noun also takes the accusative -t: azt a lányt. Literally: Ismered azt a lányt? = “know-you(DEF) that-ACC the girl-ACC?”.

question: Egy könyvet ___. (I'm reading a book)
explanation: An indefinite object (egy könyvet) takes the indefinite conjugation: olvasok. Literally: Egy könyvet olvasok. = “a book-ACC read-I”.

question: A könyvet ___. (I'm reading the book)
explanation: A definite object (a könyvet) takes the definite conjugation: olvasom. Literally: A könyvet olvasom. = “the book-ACC read-I(DEF)”.

question: Látom az ___. (I see the car)
explanation: The direct object takes -t: autó → autót. Literally: Látom az autót. = “see-I(DEF) the car-ACC”.

question: Olvasom az ___. (I'm reading the newspaper)
explanation: After a consonant, many nouns need a linking vowel before -t: újság → újságot (back vowels → -ot). Literally: Olvasom az újságot. = “read-I(DEF) the newspaper-ACC”.

question: Látom a ___. (I see the city)
explanation: Nouns ending in -s take -t directly, with no linking vowel: város → várost. Literally: Látom a várost. = “see-I(DEF) the city-ACC”.

question: Ő kávét ___. (He drinks coffee)
explanation: Inni is an -ik verb: iszom, iszol, iszik. Literally: Ő kávét iszik. = “he/she coffee-ACC drinks”.

question: A ___ alszanak. (The cats are sleeping)
explanation: The plural -k attaches directly after a vowel, and a lengthens to á: macska → macskák. Literally: A macskák alszanak. = “the cat-PL sleep-they”.

question: A ___ nyitva vannak. (The windows are open)
explanation: Plural with a linking vowel: ablak → ablakok (back vowels). Literally: A ablakok nyitva vannak. = “the window-PL open are-they”.

question: Ezek a ___ szépek. (These flowers are beautiful)
explanation: After ezek (these), the noun is plural: virág → virágok. Literally: Ezek a virágok szépek. = “these the flower-PL beautiful-PL”.

question: Budapest ___, mint Szeged. (Budapest is bigger than Szeged)
explanation: Comparative: adjective + -bb / -abb / -obb (nagy → nagyobb); “than” = mint. Literally: Budapest nagyobb, mint Szeged. = “Budapest bigger, than Szeged”.

question: Ez a ___ hely. (This is the most beautiful place)
explanation: Superlative: leg- + comparative (szebb → legszebb). Literally: Ez a legszebb hely. = “this the most-beautiful place”.

question: Nincs ___. (I have no time)
explanation: Possession: idő + -m = “my time”; nincs means “there isn't”. Literally: Nincs időm. = “isn't time-my”.

question: A film nyolc___ kezdődik. (The film starts at eight)
explanation: -kor means “at (a clock time)”. Literally: A film nyolckor kezdődik. = “the film eight-at begins”.

question: ___ érkezik a vonat? (When does the train arrive?)
explanation: Mikor = when, miért = why, hol = where. Literally: Mikor érkezik a vonat? = “when arrives the train?”.

question: ___ ide! (Come here! (informal))
explanation: The imperative of jönni is irregular: gyere (you), jöjjön (formal). Literally: Gyere ide! = “come here!”.

question: What does “hétvége” mean?
explanation: “hétvége” means “weekend”. Literally: A hétvégén pihenek. = “the weekend-on rest-I”.

question: What does “munka” mean?
explanation: “munka” means “work / job”. Literally: Sok munkám van. = “much work-my is”.

question: What does “szoba” mean?
explanation: “szoba” means “room”. Literally: A szobám kicsi. = “the room-my small”.

question: What does “család” mean?
explanation: “család” means “family”. Literally: A családom nagy. = “the family-my big”.

question: What does “kedves” mean?
explanation: “kedves” means “kind / dear”. Literally: A nagymamám nagyon kedves. = “the grandmother-my very kind”.

question: What does “mindig” mean?
explanation: “mindig” means “always”. Literally: Mindig korán kelek. = “always early get-up-I”.

question: What does “soha” mean?
explanation: “soha” means “never”. Used together with nem. Literally: Soha nem iszom kávét. = “never not drink-I coffee-ACC”.

question: What does “néha” mean?
explanation: “néha” means “sometimes”. Literally: Néha moziba megyek. = “sometimes cinema-into go-I”.

question: What does “korán” mean?
explanation: “korán” means “early”. Literally: Korán reggelizem. = “early have-breakfast-I”.

question: What does “vásárolni” mean?
explanation: “vásárolni” means “to shop / buy”. Literally: Szeretek vásárolni. = “like-I shop-to”.

question: What does “segíteni” mean?
explanation: “segíteni” means “to help”. Literally: Tudsz segíteni? = “can-you help-to”.

question: What does “ajándék” mean?
explanation: “ajándék” means “gift”. Literally: Ez egy ajándék neked. = “this a gift you-for”.

question: What does “Hogy hívják ezt magyarul?” mean?
options: How do you say this in English?
explanation: “Hogy hívják ezt magyarul?” means “What's this called in Hungarian?”. Literally: Hogy hívják ezt magyarul? = “how call-they this-ACC Hungarian-in”.

question: What does “Kérem a számlát.” mean?
explanation: “Kérem a számlát.” means “The bill, please.”. Literally: Kérem a számlát. = “ask-I the bill-ACC”.

question: What does “Szeretnék egy asztalt foglalni.” mean?
options: I'd like to see the menu.
I'd like to book a table.
explanation: “Szeretnék egy asztalt foglalni.” means “I'd like to book a table.”. Literally: Szeretnék egy asztalt foglalni. = “like-would-I a table-ACC reserve-to”.

question: What does “Forduljon balra!” mean?
explanation: “Forduljon balra!” means “Turn left! (formal)”. Literally: Forduljon balra! = “turn-you(FORM) left-to”.

question: What does “Mindjárt jövök.” mean?
explanation: “Mindjárt jövök.” means “I'll be right back.”. Literally: Mindjárt jövök. = “right-away come-I”.

question: What does “Sok sikert!” mean?
explanation: “Sok sikert!” means “Good luck!”. Literally: Sok sikert! = “much success-ACC”.

question: What does “Nem baj.” mean?
explanation: “Nem baj.” means “It doesn't matter.”. Literally: Nem baj. = “not trouble”.

question: What does “Segítségre van szükségem.” mean?
explanation: “Segítségre van szükségem.” means “I need help.”. Literally: Segítségre van szükségem. = “help-for is need-my”.

question: Ha lenne időm, többet ___. (If I had time, I'd read more)
explanation: Conditional: stem + -nék / -nék (I): olvas → olvasnék. Literally: Ha lenne időm, többet olvasnék. = “if were time-my, more-ACC read-would-I”.

question: ___ egy kávét. (I'd like a coffee)
explanation: The conditional (kérnék) makes a request more polite. Literally: Kérnék egy kávét. = “ask-would-I a coffee-ACC”.

question: Ha gazdag lennék, ___ egy házat. (If I were rich, I would buy a house)
explanation: Conditional of venni: vennék (an irregular stem). Literally: Ha gazdag lennék, vennék egy házat. = “if rich would-be-I, buy-would-I a house-ACC”.
phrase: Ha gazdag lennék, vennék egy házat.

question: Ha tudtam volna, eljöttem ___. (If I had known, I would have come)
explanation: Past unreal condition: past tense + volna in both clauses. Literally: Ha tudtam volna, eljöttem volna. = “if knew-I would, away-came-I would”.

question: ___ be! (Come in! (formal))
explanation: The formal imperative uses the -jön form: jöjjön. Literally: Jöjjön be! = “come-you(FORM) in!”.

question: Ne ___! (Don't go!)
explanation: Negative imperative: ne + imperative form (menni → menj). Literally: Ne menj! = “not go!”.

question: Azt akarom, hogy el___ a bulira. (I want you to come to the party)
explanation: After akarni hogy, use the subjunctive (imperative form): jönni → jöjj. Literally: Azt akarom, hogy eljöjj a bulira. = “that-ACC want-I that away-come-you the party-onto”.
phrase: Azt akarom, hogy eljöjj a bulira.

question: Itt nem ___ dohányozni. (You can't smoke here)
explanation: “Lehet” means “it is possible”; nem lehet means “it is not allowed”. Literally: Itt nem lehet dohányozni. = “here not is-possible smoke-to”.

question: Segít___? (May I help you?)
explanation: The suffix -het/-hat expresses possibility or permission: segít + het + ek. Literally: Segíthetek? = “help-may-I?”.

question: Korán ___ kelnem. (I have to get up early)
explanation: Kell + infinitive (with a personal ending) means “must / have to”. Literally: Korán kell kelnem. = “early must get-up-to-my”.

question: Már ___ a levelet. (I've already written the letter)
explanation: The prefix meg- marks a completed action: megírtam. Literally: Már megírtam a levelet. = “already PREVERB-wrote-I the letter-ACC”.

question: Nem ___ meg a leckét. (I haven't done the homework)
explanation: In negation, the preverb moves behind the verb: nem csináltam meg. Literally: Nem csináltam meg a leckét. = “not did-I PREVERB the homework-ACC”.

question: A ___ itt vannak. (Our friends are here)
explanation: Plural possessed noun: barát + -aink = our friends. Literally: A barátaink itt vannak. = “the friend-our-PL here are-they”.

question: Hol van a ___? (Where is your bag? (informal))
explanation: Possessive -d means “your” (informal): táska → táskád. Literally: Hol van a táskád? = “where is the bag-your?”.

question: ___ ez a könyv? (Whose is this book?)
explanation: “Kié” asks “whose is it?”. Literally: Kié ez a könyv? = “whose this the book?”.

question: Adok egy ajándékot a nővérem___. (I'm giving a present to my sister)
explanation: -nak/-nek marks the recipient (dative): nővérem + nek. Literally: Adok egy ajándékot a nővéremnek. = “give-I a present-ACC the sister-my-to”.

question: Péter___ van egy autója. (Péter has a car)
explanation: A possessor takes -nak/-nek and the thing owned takes a possessive suffix: Péternek van egy autója. Literally: Péternek van egy autója. = “Péter-to is a car-his”.

question: Nem ismerek ___. (I don't know anyone)
explanation: Negative pronouns take -t as objects (senki → senkit), and Hungarian needs nem as well. Literally: Nem ismerek senkit. = “not know-I nobody-ACC”.

question: Nem látok ___. (I can't see anything)
explanation: Semmi (nothing) takes -t as an object: semmit; the verb also needs nem. Literally: Nem látok semmit. = “not see-I nothing-ACC”.

question: A ház, ___ ott áll, nagyon régi. (The house that stands there is very old)
explanation: “Ami” is the relative pronoun for things; “aki” is for people. Literally: A ház, ami ott áll, nagyon régi. = “the house, which there stands, very old”.
phrase: A ház, ami ott áll, nagyon régi.

question: A férfi, ___ ott áll, a tanárom. (The man standing there is my teacher)
explanation: “Aki” refers to people. Literally: A férfi, aki ott áll, a tanárom. = “the man, who there stands, the teacher-my”.
phrase: A férfi, aki ott áll, a tanárom.

question: Jól érzem ___ itt. (I feel good here)
explanation: The reflexive pronoun agrees with the subject: én → magam. Literally: Jól érzem magam itt. = “well feel-I myself here”.

question: Szeretik ___. (They love each other)
explanation: “Egymás” (each other) takes -t as an object: egymást. Literally: Szeretik egymást. = “love-they(DEF) each-other-ACC”.

question: Ő magasabb ___. (He's taller than me)
explanation: “Than me” can be expressed with nál- + a personal ending: nálam. Literally: Ő magasabb nálam. = “he/she taller me-than”.

question: Nyolc___ dolgozom. (I work until eight)
explanation: -ig means “until / as far as”. Literally: Nyolcig dolgozom. = “eight-until work-I”.

question: Hétfő___ péntekig dolgozom. (I work from Monday to Friday)
explanation: -tól/-től … -ig means “from … to”. Literally: Hétfőtől péntekig dolgozom. = “Monday-from Friday-until work-I”.

question: Köszönöm a segítség___. (Thank you for the help)
explanation: -ért means “for (the sake of)”: segítségért. Literally: Köszönöm a segítségért. = “thank-I the help-for”.

question: Orvos___ akar válni. (He wants to become a doctor)
explanation: -vá/-vé (“becoming”) assimilates after a consonant: orvos + vá → orvossá. Literally: Orvossá akar válni. = “doctor-into wants become-to”.

question: ___ tanulsz magyarul? (How long have you been learning Hungarian?)
explanation: “Mióta” asks “since when / how long (up to now)?”. Literally: Mióta tanulsz magyarul? = “since-when learn-you Hungarian-in?”.

question: Te ___ a levest? (Do you eat the soup?)
explanation: With a definite object (a levest), enni takes definite endings: eszem, eszed, eszi. Literally: Te eszed a levest? = “you eat-you(DEF) the soup-ACC?”.

question: What does “azonban” mean?
explanation: “azonban” means “however”. Literally: Szeretnék jönni, azonban dolgozom. = “like-would-I come-to, however work-I”.

question: What does “viszont” mean?
explanation: “viszont” means “on the other hand / but”. Literally: Ő magas, én viszont alacsony vagyok. = “he/she tall, I on-the-other-hand short am-I”.
phrase: Ő magas, én viszont alacsony vagyok.

question: What does “ráadásul” mean?
explanation: “ráadásul” means “moreover / on top of that”. Literally: Drága, ráadásul rossz. = “expensive, moreover bad”.

question: What does “mégis” mean?
explanation: “mégis” means “nevertheless / yet”. Literally: Esett az eső, mégis elmentünk. = “fell the rain, nevertheless away-went-we”.

question: What does “tehát” mean?
explanation: “tehát” means “so / therefore”. Literally: Sietnem kell, tehát megyek. = “hurry-to-my must, therefore go-I”.

question: What does “állás” mean?
explanation: “állás” means “job / position”. Also means “standing” or “score”. Literally: Új állást keresek. = “new job-ACC seek-I”.

question: What does “fizetés” mean?
explanation: “fizetés” means “salary / payment”. Literally: A fizetés hónap végén érkezik. = “the salary month end-at arrives”.

question: What does “önéletrajz” mean?
explanation: “önéletrajz” means “CV / résumé”. Literally “self-life-drawing”. Literally: Elküldtem az önéletrajzomat. = “sent-I the CV-my-ACC”.

question: What does “csalódott” mean?
explanation: “csalódott” means “disappointed”. Literally: Csalódott vagyok az eredmény miatt. = “disappointed am-I the result because-of”.

question: What does “környezet” mean?
explanation: “környezet” means “environment / surroundings”. Literally: Védenünk kell a környezetet. = “protect-we-must the environment-ACC”.

question: What does “megbeszélés” mean?
explanation: “megbeszélés” means “meeting / discussion”. Literally: Holnap megbeszélésünk van. = “tomorrow meeting-our is”.

question: What does “elkésni” mean?
options: to be late / to miss (by being late)
explanation: “elkésni” means “to be late / to miss (by being late)”. The thing missed takes -ról/-ről. Literally: Elkéstem a vonatról. = “late-was-I the train-from”.

question: What does “Nem tehetek róla.” mean?
explanation: “Nem tehetek róla.” means “I can't help it.”. Literally: Nem tehetek róla. = “not do-can-I it-about”.

question: What does “Mindegy.” mean?
explanation: “Mindegy.” means “Whatever / It doesn't matter.”. Literally: Mindegy. = “all-same”.

question: What does “Szerintem igazad van.” mean?
explanation: “Szerintem igazad van.” means “I think you're right.”. Literally: Szerintem igazad van. = “according-to-me right-your is”.

question: What does “Sajnos nem tudok jönni.” mean?
explanation: “Sajnos nem tudok jönni.” means “Unfortunately I can't come.”. Literally: Sajnos nem tudok jönni. = “unfortunately not can-I come-to”.

question: What does “Ömlik az eső.” mean?
explanation: “Ömlik az eső.” means “It's pouring.”. Literally: Ömlik az eső. = “pours the rain”.

question: What does “Köszönöm a meghívást.” mean?
explanation: “Köszönöm a meghívást.” means “Thank you for the invitation.”. Literally: Köszönöm a meghívást. = “thank-I the invitation-ACC”.

question: What does “Hamarosan találkozunk.” mean?
explanation: “Hamarosan találkozunk.” means “See you soon.”. Literally: Hamarosan találkozunk. = “soon meet-we”.

question: What does “Jobbulást!” mean?
explanation: “Jobbulást!” means “Get well soon!”. Literally: Jobbulást! = “betterment-ACC”.

question: Ha korábban ___ volna, elértük volna a vonatot. (If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train)
explanation: Past unreal condition: past tense + volna in both clauses. Literally: Ha korábban indultunk volna, elértük volna a vonatot. = “if earlier left-we would, reached-we would the train-ACC”.
phrase: Ha korábban indultunk volna, elértük volna a vonatot.

question: Kérem, hogy ___ csendben. (Please be quiet (said to several people))
explanation: After kérni hogy, the subjunctive is used: lenni → legyenek. Literally: Kérem, hogy legyenek csendben. = “ask-I that be-they quiet-in”.

question: Fontos, hogy időben ___. (It's important that you arrive on time)
explanation: After expressions of necessity + hogy, use the subjunctive: érkezz. Literally: Fontos, hogy időben érkezz. = “important, that time-in arrive-you”.

question: Az ajtó mellett ___ férfi a testvérem. (The man standing by the door is my brother)
explanation: The present participle -ó/-ő works like an adjective: áll → álló. Literally: Az ajtó mellett álló férfi a testvérem. = “the door next-to standing man the sibling-my”.
phrase: Az ajtó mellett álló férfi a testvérem.

question: A tegnap ___ levél az asztalon van. (The letter written yesterday is on the table)
explanation: The past participle -t / -ott describes a completed action: megírt. Literally: A tegnap megírt levél az asztalon van. = “the yesterday PREVERB-written letter the table-on is”.
phrase: A tegnap megírt levél az asztalon van.

question: Zenét ___ tanul. (He studies while listening to music)
explanation: The adverbial participle -va/-ve means “while / by doing”. Literally: Zenét hallgatva tanul. = “music-ACC listening studies”.

question: Azt ___, hogy holnap esni fog. (They say it will rain tomorrow)
explanation: After azt (a definite object), the verb takes the definite form: mondják (they say). Literally: Azt mondják, hogy holnap esni fog. = “that-ACC say-they(DEF), that tomorrow fall-to will”.
phrase: Azt mondják, hogy holnap esni fog.

question: Azt ___, hogy igaza van. (I think he's right)
explanation: Azt (“that”) is a definite object, so the verb takes the definite form: hiszem. Literally: Azt hiszem, hogy igaza van. = “that-ACC believe-I(DEF), that right-his is”.

question: Bárcsak ___ időm! (If only I had time!)
explanation: “Bárcsak” (if only) is followed by the conditional. Literally: Bárcsak lenne időm! = “if-only would-be time-my!”.

question: Annak ellenére, hogy fáradt ___, tovább dolgozott. (Although he was tired, he kept working)
explanation: “Annak ellenére, hogy” (although) takes the indicative; here the past: volt. Literally: Annak ellenére, hogy fáradt volt, tovább dolgozott. = “that-to contrary, that tired was, further worked”.
phrase: Annak ellenére, hogy fáradt volt, tovább dolgozott.

question: Miután ___ a vacsorát, sétálni mentünk. (After we had eaten dinner, we went for a walk)
explanation: “Miután” (after) takes the past tense; with a definite object: megettük. Literally: Miután megettük a vacsorát, sétálni mentünk. = “after PREVERB-ate-we(DEF) the dinner-ACC, walk-to went-we”.
phrase: Miután megettük a vacsorát, sétálni mentünk.

question: Mielőtt ___, kapcsold ki a lámpát. (Before you leave, turn off the light)
explanation: “Mielőtt” (before) is followed by the present for a future action. Literally: Mielőtt elmész, kapcsold ki a lámpát. = “before away-go-you, switch off the lamp-ACC”.
phrase: Mielőtt elmész, kapcsold ki a lámpát.

question: Várok, amíg ___. (I'll wait until you come back)
explanation: “Amíg” (until) + a perfective present expresses a future event. Literally: Várok, amíg visszajössz. = “wait-I, until back-come-you”.

question: Reggelente futni ___. (I usually go running in the mornings)
explanation: “Szokni” + infinitive expresses habit: szoktam (I). Literally: Reggelente futni szoktam. = “mornings-in run-to am-accustomed-I”.

question: Már ___ a hideget. (I'm already used to the cold)
explanation: Meg- + szokni means “to get used to”; the thing takes the accusative. Literally: Már megszoktam a hideget. = “already PREVERB-got-used-I the cold-ACC”.

question: Hajat ___. (I'm having my hair cut)
explanation: The causative -at/-et means “to have something done”: vág → vágat. Literally: Hajat vágatok. = “hair-ACC cut-cause-I”.

question: Szeretném, ha gyorsabb ___. (I'd like you to be faster)
explanation: “Szeretném, ha …” (I'd like it if …) takes the conditional: lennél. Literally: Szeretném, ha gyorsabb lennél. = “like-would-I(DEF), if faster would-be-you”.

question: A ház ___ áll egy fa. (There's a tree in front of the house)
explanation: Postpositions follow the noun: a ház előtt = in front of the house. Literally: A ház előtt áll egy fa. = “the house in-front-of stands a tree”.
phrase: A ház előtt áll egy fa.

question: ___ állt valaki. (Someone was standing behind me)
explanation: Postpositions take personal endings: mögött + em → mögöttem. Literally: Mögöttem állt valaki. = “behind-me stood somebody”.

question: Beszélek ___. (I'm talking to him/her)
explanation: -val/-vel with a personal ending becomes vele (with him/her). Literally: Beszélek vele. = “speak-I him/her-with”.

question: Nem kávét, ___ teát kérek. (I'm asking for tea, not coffee)
explanation: “Hanem” (but rather) follows a negative statement: nem … hanem … Literally: Nem kávét, hanem teát kérek. = “not coffee-ACC, but tea-ACC ask-I”.

question: Sem kávét, ___ teát nem iszom. (I drink neither coffee nor tea)
explanation: “Sem … sem …” means “neither … nor …”, with nem before the verb. Literally: Sem kávét, sem teát nem iszom. = “neither coffee-ACC, nor tea-ACC not drink-I”.
phrase: Sem kávét, sem teát nem iszom.

question: Három éve ___ itt. (I've been living here for three years)
explanation: Duration + “éve” takes the present tense: három éve élek itt. Literally: Három éve élek itt. = “three year-ago live-I here”.

question: Hetente ___ sportolok. (I do sports three times a week)
explanation: -szor/-szer/-ször means “times”: három → háromszor. Literally: Hetente háromszor sportolok. = “weekly three-times do-sports-I”.

question: Május ___ van a születésnapom. (My birthday is on the 5th of May)
explanation: Dates use an ordinal number + -án/-én: ötödike → ötödikén. Literally: Május ötödikén van a születésnapom. = “May fifth-on is the birthday-my”.

question: Nem tudom, otthon ___. (I don't know whether he's at home)
explanation: The particle -e is attached to the verb in indirect yes/no questions: van-e. Literally: Nem tudom, otthon van-e. = “not know-I, home is-whether”.

question: Ne ___ el senkinek! (Don't tell anyone! (informal))
explanation: With an implied definite object, the imperative takes the definite form: mondd. Literally: Ne mondd el senkinek! = “not tell(DEF) away nobody-to!”.

question: ___ gondolok. (I'm thinking of you (informal))
explanation: Gondolni takes -ra/-re; with a personal ending: rád (“onto you”, i.e. of you). Literally: Rád gondolok. = “you-onto think-I”.

question: What does “ugyanakkor” mean?
options: at the same time / on the other hand
explanation: “ugyanakkor” means “at the same time / on the other hand”. Literally: Ez jó ötlet, ugyanakkor kockázatos. = “this good idea, at-the-same-time risky”.

question: What does “ennek ellenére” mean?
explanation: “ennek ellenére” means “in spite of this”. Literally: Fáradt volt, ennek ellenére dolgozott. = “tired was, this-to contrary worked”.

question: What does “kihívás” mean?
explanation: “kihívás” means “challenge”. Literally: Ez nagy kihívás számomra. = “this big challenge me-for”.

question: What does “fejlődés” mean?
explanation: “fejlődés” means “development / progress”. Literally: A fejlődés lassú, de biztos. = “the progress slow, but sure”.

question: What does “tapasztalat” mean?
explanation: “tapasztalat” means “experience”. Literally: Sok tapasztalatom van. = “much experience-my is”.

question: What does “döntés” mean?
